newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SEC probing variable annuity sales practices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SEC probing variable annuity sales practices.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is probing the variable annuity sales practices at over a dozen insurers, an SEC official said.
Gene Gohlke, associate director for compliance at the SEC, called the probe a routine inspection and said he was not yet aware of any specific abuses by any of the companies.
"We're just looking at these practices to see if, in fact, they're out there," Gohlke said.
Thirteen companies are involved in the inspection, Gohlke said. Aetna Inc confirmed it was among those companies under inspection.
Mark Mackey, president of the National Association for Variable Annuities, said he believed most, if not all, of the companies being inspected distribute their products through captive sales forces.
Gohlke said the SEC is looking into practices that encourage policyholders to exchange one variable annuity product for another, generating a new commission for the sales agent.
The inspection also is looking at the refinancing of life insurance policies.
Under this practice, an agent persuades a policyholder to take out a second policy and use the cash value of the first to pay the premiums on the second, again generating a new commission.
"We're not saying all refinancing is inappropriate," Gohlke said. "But, is there an excess amount of it?"
Gohlke said the SEC began the inspection in December and does not know when it will be completed.
Mackey believes the inspections are a result of the rapid growth in the variable annuity industry.
"As the industry has grown, it's going to receive more attention," Mackey said.

"We certainly support the SEC in carrying out these inspections," he said. "Consumers take a great deal of comfort, justifiably, in knowing that the SEC regulates the financial markets. That gives them confidence in the industry," he said.
